title: Messaging between popup, content script and service worker
when: Parts of a browser extension must talk to each other: the popup asks the page for data, or a content script asks the service worker to fetch or store something.
prompt:
Goal: Typed messages, one router per context, async replies that always arrive, sender checks, and clear handling when nobody listens.
Steps:
1. Shape: { type: "page/getTitle", payload }; all types listed in messages.js and shared by every part.
2. Popup to worker: const reply = await chrome.runtime.sendMessage({ type: "data/save", payload }).
3. To a page: await chrome.tabs.sendMessage(tabId, msg); only tabs running the content script receive it.
4. Router: chrome.runtime.onMessage.addListener((msg, sender, sendResponse) => { const h = handlers[msg?.type]; if (!h) return false; Promise.resolve().then(() => h(msg.payload, sender)).then((r) => sendResponse({ ok: true, r }), (e) => sendResponse({ ok: false, error: String(e) })); return true; }); return true keeps the channel open.
5. The worker accepts only sender.id === chrome.runtime.id.
6. "Receiving end does not exist" means no listener: catch it and inject the script or show a hint.
7. Streams: chrome.runtime.connect({ name: "progress" }) with port.onMessage and port.onDisconnect.
Quality bar:
- Every request gets exactly one reply.
- Unknown types are ignored, not thrown.
Pitfalls:
- An async listener: it returns a promise instead of true, so the reply may never arrive.
- Trusting window.postMessage from pages without checking origin and shape.
Verify:
- [ ] Shared type list.
- [ ] Router returns true for async replies.
- [ ] sender.id checked.
- [ ] Missing receiver handled.
Output: messages.js, routers in background.js and content.js, and the calls in popup.js.

examples.input: o popup precisa pegar o titulo da pagina pelo content script
examples.output: messages.js type list, router with return true and sendResponse, sender.id check, Receiving end does not exist handled in popup.js
